nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ru/NiV-LDH family
nodes.procedure: RuCl3·xH2O (62 mg, corresponding to 0.3 mmol) was initially dissolved in 30 mL DI water containing 120 mg urea. This aqueous solution was subsequently blended with 10 mL ethylene glycol solution containing 349 mg Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 47.2 mg VCl3. The resultant mixture, along with a pretreated nickel foam substrate (2 cm × 4 cm), was hydrothermally processed in a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave at 120 °C for 12 h. The obtained Ru/NiV-LDH was then vacuum-dried at 60 °C overnight. For comparative analysis, control samples with varying ruthenium loadings were prepared by adjusting RuCl3·xH2O quantities to 0.025 mmol (5.19 mg), 0.05 mmol (10.37 mg), 0.2 mmol (41.5 mg), and 0.4 mmol (83 mg) while maintaining identical synthesis parameters. The corresponding samples are named Ru0.025/NiV-LDH, Ru0.05/NiV-LDH, Ru0.2/NiV-LDH, Ru0.3/NiV-LDH and Ru0.4/NiV-LDH, respectively. NiV-LDH was also prepared without Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/V-NiO, V-NiO, and NiO catalysts exhibit diffraction peaks at 37.09°, 43.10°, 62.59°, 75.04°, and 79.01° corresponding to the (111), (200), (220), (311), and (222) crystal planes of NiO (PDF#03-065-6920). No diffraction peaks for Ru, V, or their oxides detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After being subjected to annealing treatment, the result NiO, V-NiO, Ru/V-NiO, Ru/V-NiO-300, and Ru/V-NiO-400 catalysts exhibit diffraction peaks at 37.09°, 43.10°, 62.59°, 75.04°, and 79.01°, which relate to the (111), (200), (220), (311), and (222) crystal planes of the NiO (PDF#03–065–6920), respectively (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/V-NiO shows nanoplatelet-like porous structure consisting of interconnected nanoparticles. The nanosheet-like hierarchical structure becomes loose and porous between 300-400°C annealing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Fig. 1d and Fig. S7, the SEM morphology of Ru/V-NiO is affected by the annealing temperature. Within the range of 300 °C to 400 °C, the nanosheet-like hierarchical structure becomes increasingly loose and porous.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/V-NiO nanoplatelet-like porous structure consists of interconnected nanoparticles. Lattice spacings of 0.209 nm and 0.201 nm ascribed to NiO (200) and Ru (101) facets. SAED shows NiO (220) and Ru (101) rings.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1e, the nanoplatelet-like porous structure of Ru/V-NiO consists of a large number of interconnected nanoparticles... The observed lattice spacings of 0.209 nm and 0.201 nm are ascribed to the (200) facet of NiO and the (101) facet of Ru, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Distinct lattice fringes visible with spacings of 0.209 nm (NiO (200)) and 0.201 nm (Ru (101)).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, distinct lattice fringes of Ru/V-NiO are clearly visible in the high-resolution electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images (Fig. 1f and Fig. S10a-f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ni, V, O; Ru broadly dispersed across nanoplatelet-like porous structure surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) imaging (Fig. S11 and Fig. 1g-k) displays the spatial distribution of Ni, V, O, and Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/V-NiO Ni 2p peaks: 855.23/872.96 eV (Ni²⁺ 2p3/2,1/2), 857.24/875.65 eV (Ni³⁺ 2p3/2,1/2); V 2p3/2: 515.83 eV (V³⁺), 516.65 eV (V⁴⁺), 517.50 eV (V⁵⁺) with 0.10 eV positive shift vs V-NiO; Ru 3p: 462.18/484.41 eV (Ru⁰); O 1s: 529.92 eV (M-O), 531.00 eV (unsaturated O), 533.06 eV (adsorbed O). Positive BE shifts confirm interfacial charge redistribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2b illustrates that the dominant peaks in the Ni 2p spectra for Ru/V-NiO can be deconvoluted into four subpeaks. The two sharp peaks at 855.23 and 872.96 eV are assigned to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 of Ni²⁺, while the peaks at 857.24 and 875.65 eV correspond to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 of Ni³⁺... The high-resolution V 2p3/2 spectrum... can be deconvoluted into three binding energy components, corresponding to V3+ 2p3/2, V4+ 2p3/2 and V5+ 2p3/2, with binding energies of 515.83, 516.65, and 517.50 eV, respectively.
